mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a flattening industrial production trend (INDPRO stable) indicates weakening consumer demand without supply shock, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND INDPRO monthly change within ±0.2% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predictive accuracy drops below 40% out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to reduced consumer spending and margin compression.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months, absent a corresponding decline in capacity utilization (not available), suggests supply-side contraction that raises input costs and reduces earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust across recessions and expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a six-month window signals a deflationary monetary easing, which historically increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (p > 0.10), or the effect reverses in high-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive monthly growth in personal income (not available) or, as a proxy, a concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) signals robust demand expansion, which predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (p > 0.10), or the effect disappears in late-cycle conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between the year-over-year growth in real GDP (GDPC1) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns; higher GDP growth is associated with higher near-term equity gains due to improved earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 YoY growth and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
